title: LLM routing + KV prefetch PRD scratchpad
content:
TL;DR:
- Rough PRD draft for: smart routing + KV prefetch to reduce tail latency and per-token cost for common prefixes (chat apps, assistants, completion-heavy flows).
- Idea: route requests to cheapest compatible model that still meets latency/quality SLOs, and opportunistically prefetch KV cache for likely next-turn prefixes on long-running sessions.
- Benefits: lower median/tail latency for hot sessions, fewer tokens executed on bigger models, lower GPU token cost via cache hits.

Problem statement / motivation:
- Many customers report spiky tails when users open long conversations or paste long system prompts. Serving runtime rebuilds KV cache on new model instances and cold sessions -> repeated recompute.
- We have opportunity to: 1) route to smaller model variant when quality acceptable, 2) avoid repeated attention computation via prefetching/populating KV cache for likely prefixes.
- Target workloads: chat assistants, code completion, multi-turn Q&A.

Goals (MVP):
- Implement a routing policy that considers model variant compatibility + recent quality telemetry to select candidate model(s) for a request.
- Add a lightweight KV prefetch helper that can populate new model instances with most-likely next-token/key-values for active sessions (best-effort, non-blocking).
- Measure latency (p50/p95/p99), cost-per-response (tokens on large model), and quality regression delta (BLEU/embedding-similarity on sample prompts).

Success metrics (initial):
- p95 latency reduction for multi-turn chat flows by >= 15% over baseline.
- Per-response GPU token cost reduction >= 10% for top-10 customers in pilot.
- No quality regressions > 1% on curated eval prompt set (prompt-set: routing-prefetch-eval-v1).

User stories / personas:
- Engineer (Startup product) -> "I want consistent latencies for my chat users during peak, without rewriting prompts or forcing a single model version."
- Platform engineer -> "I want routing policies to be declarative and observable, and to allow safe fallbacks to larger models when quality issues are detected."
- SRE -> "I want prefetching to be safe (no noisy spikes), optional per-customer, and with throttles to avoid overloading GPUs."

Proposed approach (high-level):
1) Routing policy layer updates:
   - Add candidate ranking: [preferred lightweight variant, fallback to heavier variant if QoS fails].
   - Policy inputs: customer tier, latency SLO, model compatibility map, recent eval signals (quality regressions), route tags (sensitive/regulatory => force pinned model).
   - Quick scoring function: score = w1*predicted_latency + w2*predicted_cost + w3*quality_penalty. Tunable defaults.

2) KV prefetch subsystem (MVP):
   - When a session is active and observed prefix matches known patterns (greetings, system prompt, instruction templates), in background issue prefetch tokens to new model instance(s) to populate KV cache.
   - Prefetch should be: best-effort, capped per-session and per-customer, cancelable, and idempotent.
   - Prefetch triggers: opening a new connection, model switch, canary rollout, scaled-up replica.

3) Observability and safety:
   - Expose per-route metrics: prefetch hit-rate, prefetch token overhead, latency delta when prefetch hit vs miss, routing decisions log (model chosen and score).
   - Automatic rollback/disable if quality regressions above threshold.

Technical considerations / risks:
- Prefetch correctness: must not change semantic output; only affects performance. But prefetching could inadvertently alter randomness/state in generative models (seed/state). Need to ensure prefetch only builds deterministic KV cache without advancing RNG/state visible to final generation. Work with runtime team.
- Cost tradeoffs: prefetch issues extra tokens on warmup. Need conservative caps and cost accounting. Could be expensive if mis-triggered.
- Compatibility: quantized/compiled model variants may have different KV layout; prefetch only for compatible variants.
- Security / privacy: prefetch should respect KMS and data residency; do not persist cross-customer secrets in shared caches.
- Backpressure: prefetch requests should be low-priority and throttled under load.

Experiments (pilot):
- Phase A (internal): run on 3 internal workloads (chat-bot-sim, code-complete-sim, doc-QA) comparing baseline vs routing-only vs routing+prefetch. Collect latency, cost, quality.
- Phase B (customer pilot): 2 customers opt-in, traffic shadowed with enabling prefetch and routing (no live change) for 2 weeks, then canary ~5% traffic for 1 week.

Rollout plan (sketch):
- Week 0-2: implement scoring + simple routing policy + observability.
- Week 3-6: build prefetch controller + safety hooks + throttles.
- Week 7-12: internal pilot, iterate.
- Post-week 12: customer pilots + gated rollout (per-customer opt-in).

Open questions / unresolved: 
- How to compute "likely next prefixes" efficiently? Options: n-gram freq table per-route, small next-token predictor model, or heuristics based on prompt templates. Tradeoffs: accuracy vs runtime cost.
- What is the right default cap on prefetch tokens per session? 64? 128? Need experiment.
- Interaction with streaming: if we stream partial responses while prefetch still populating, could that introduce inconsistency. Need to define ordering guarantees.
- Should routing be per-request or per-session sticky? Likely start per-request with sticky hints for sessions.

Immediate TODOs (short):
- Draft evaluation prompt set (routing-prefetch-eval-v1). @Aisha to pick 200 prompts across chat/code/doc flows.
- Design prefetch idempotency API with runtime (Jordan).
- Wire basic routing scoring telemetry in console (Emma).
- Create JIRA tickets for infra quotas, metrics dashboard, and privacy review (INF-XXXX placeholders).

Notes to self / brainstorming fragments:
- Could combine with model-quantization-aware routing: route to quantized model for low-cost but only for short outputs.
- Consider caching by customer + prompt-hash to avoid cross-customer leakage and reduce duplicate prefetch.
- If prefetch hit rate > 60% and cost delta < 15%, consider enabling by default for trial customers.

References / linked ideas:
- CONFLUENCE: routing-policy-templates (link above)
- JIRA: INF-4821 is previous work on "fast fallback"; reuse code for scoring.
- GH PR: runtime prefetch prototype (see linked PR).

Next steps (this week):
- Sync with runtime on prefetch safety (Jordan) - ask: can we prepopulate KV without altering RNG/state?
- Quick prototype: implement simple heuristic prefetch (prefix templates + capped tokens). Measure cost.
- Put together pilot metric dashboard spec (Emma).

-- end scratchpad --

(Notes are rough, expect lots of iteration. This doc will be used as a working reference for scoping a small project team.)
